title: वैदिक दर्शनमा आनन्द (सुख) को स्वरूप(Form of Ananda (happiness) in Vedic philosophy)
nepali: सुख, खुसी तथा आनन्द – यी प्रचलित शब्द हुन् , सुखले भौतिक शरीरको, खुसीले मनको र आनन्दले आत्माका गुणहरूको प्रतिनिधित्व गर्छन् ः यो वैदिक बुझाइ हो । साधारण रूपमा सुन्दा र प्रयोग गर्दा पर्यायवाचीजस्ता प्रतीत भए पनि वैदिक ऋषिमुनि र आचार्यहरूले उपर्युक्त तिनै विषयवस्तुहरूलाई फरकफरक रूपमा साक्षात्कार गरेका छन् र साक्षात्कारका विधिहरू समेतको विशद चर्चापरिचर्चा गरेका छन् । उपनिषद्हरूले जीवनको प्राथमिक लक्ष्य सुखप्राप्ति, दोस्रो लक्ष्य सुख (रस) प्राप्ति र अन्तिम लक्ष्य नै आनन्द–प्राप्तिको बाटो तोकेका छन् । यो लक्ष्यलाई कसैले आनन्द, कसैले पूर्णता, कसैले मोक्ष, कसैले, मुक्ति, कसैले परमज्ञान, कसैले निर्वाण, कसैले ब्रह्मैकत्व र कसैले अभयपदको प्राप्ति भनेका छन् । भौतिक सुख, मानसिक रस र आध्यात्मिक उत्सवका रूपमा परमानन्द वा ब्रह्मानन्दको प्राप्तिका लागि कर्म, ज्ञान र भक्ति यी तीनवटा मार्गहरू पूर्वनिश्चित छन् । जीवले आफ्नो अभिमुखीकरणका आधारमा उपर्युक्त तीनमध्ये एउटा बाटोमा आफूलाई निमज्ज गर्छ र आनन्दको लक्ष्य प्राप्त गर्छ ्र भूमा–सुखको प्राप्तिको लागि हरेक जीवले स्वतन्त्र रूपमा शारीरिक सुख, मानसिक खुसी (रस) का खुड्किलाहरू पार गर्नैपर्छ । आनन्द तेस्रो खुड्किलो हो, जहाँबाट खुड्किलाहरूको सधैँका लागि अवशान हुन्छ । निःसन्देह, दर्शनशास्त्री तथा मनोवैज्ञानिकहरूले भूमा–सुखका विषयमा चर्चा गरेका छन् तथापि शरीर र तथा मनभन्दा माथिल्लो तहको पूर्णआनन्दका विषयमा उपनिषद्हरूले बढी चर्चा गरेका छन् । शरीर र मनको सुख त महत्त्वपूर्ण छन् नै । त्यसभन्दा पनि बढी महत्त्वपूर्ण आत्माको सुख (आनन्द) छ भन्ने विषयको प्रतिष्ठा यस अनुसन्धान आलेखले स्थापित गर्ने प्रयास गरेको छ ।
american_english: Sukha, happiness and ananda — these are common words; sukha represents the qualities of the physical body, happiness those of the mind, and ananda those of the soul: this is the Vedic understanding. Although they appear synonymous when heard and used in ordinary speech, the Vedic sages and acharyas have realized the above three subjects in different forms and have also discussed in detail the methods of realization. The Upanishads have set the path of attaining sukha as the primary goal of life, attaining sukha (rasa) as the second goal, and attaining ananda as the ultimate goal. Some call this goal ananda, some completeness, some moksha, some mukti, some supreme knowledge, some nirvana, some brahmaikatva, and some the attainment of abhayapada. For the attainment of paramananda or brahmananda in the form of physical sukha, mental rasa and spiritual bliss, the three paths of karma, jnana and bhakti are predetermined. The being, on the basis of its orientation, immerses itself in one of the above three paths and attains the goal of ananda; for the attainment of bhuma-sukha, every being must independently cross the steps of physical pleasure and mental happiness (rasa). Ananda is the third step, from which the steps come to a permanent end. Undoubtedly, philosophers and psychologists have discussed bhuma-sukha, yet the Upanishads have discussed the full ananda of a level higher than the body and the mind more. The sukha of the body and the mind are certainly important. This research article has attempted to establish the subject that the sukha (ananda) of the soul is even more important than that.

informal_english: Sukha, happiness and ananda — these are everyday words; sukha stands for the qualities of the physical body, happiness for those of the mind, and ananda for those of the soul: that's the Vedic way of looking at it. They sound like synonyms when you hear and use them normally, but the Vedic sages and acharyas have actually experienced these three things in different ways and have discussed the methods of that experience in great detail. The Upanishads have set attaining sukha as the first goal of life, attaining sukha (rasa) as the second, and attaining ananda as the last. Some call this goal ananda, some completeness, some moksha, some mukti, some supreme knowledge, some nirvana, some brahmaikatva, and some the attainment of abhayapada. For getting paramananda or brahmananda as physical sukha, mental rasa and spiritual bliss, the three paths of karma, jnana and bhakti are already fixed. The being, depending on its orientation, immerses itself in one of these three paths and attains the goal of ananda; for bhuma-sukha, every being has to cross on its own the steps of physical pleasure and mental happiness (rasa). Ananda is the third step, after which the steps end for good. No doubt philosophers and psychologists have talked about bhuma-sukha, but the Upanishads have talked more about the full ananda that is above the body and the mind. The sukha of the body and the mind are important, no doubt. This research article has tried to establish that the sukha (ananda) of the soul is even more important than that.
translator_notes: Stray devanagari combining character '्र' in the source treated as a conjunctive 'and' within one sentence; informal register is Indian English.
